content: Maraviroc is a medication used in combination with other HIV treatments to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, which allows the immune system to function more effectively. This, in turn, lowers the risk of developing complications related to HIV, such as new infections or certain cancers, and improves overall quality of life. Maraviroc belongs to a class of drugs known as entry inhibitors. However, it is important to note that this medication is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, it is essential to continue taking all prescribed HIV medications as directed by your doctor. Additionally, using effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity is recommended. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids. Before starting maraviroc, it is crucial to inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies to this medication or other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Maraviroc may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Limit alcoholic beverages while taking this medication. During pregnancy, maraviroc should only be used when clearly needed. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the infection to your baby, and maraviroc may be part of this treatment plan. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. To minimize this risk, keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some products, such as orlistat, may interact with maraviroc. This document does not include all possible drug interactions, so always consult your healthcare provider for more information. If someone overdoses on maraviroc and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. It is important to attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose of maraviroc, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store maraviroc at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. This medication may rarely cause serious liver problems. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction may occur before liver issues develop. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience persistent nausea or vomiting, rash, yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, or extreme tiredness. These symptoms may indicate possible liver damage or a serious allergic reaction. As your immune system strengthens while taking maraviroc, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, leading to symptoms at any time, even months after starting HIV treatment. Notify your doctor if you experience any unusual symptoms. Common side effects of maraviroc include cough, stomach pain, tiredness, lightheadedness, or dizziness when standing. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. If you experience any severe or persistent side effects, contact your doctor promptly. This document provides a summary of information about maraviroc and does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
